world.description: Document-owned cell rows. These remain mutation-addressable through state:<name>.

name.description: A validated state-section row name or cell key — the base SafeName rule plus no dot anywhere, which is what makes the state.<row>.<key> HUD binding grammar unambiguous by construction: splitting a bound token on '.' can never mistake part of a row or cell name for a grammar separator, because neither can hold one. A row's reserved slot key ("$value") is unaffected — '$' is neither a reserved character nor a dot, so it is already a legal CellName like any other author-chosen key, exactly the one reserved exception the substrate mints rather than authors.

kind.description: The closed set of cell value kinds a state row declares, shared by every cell the row carries. Carries no float kind: simulation state is float-free by the determinism contract (see Fixed for how a fractional value still rides here). A counter is represented as Fixed; a timer is Int with NonNegative set.

cells.description: The row's current cells (default empty). Refused past its effective capacity, and on a duplicate key, by name — unless Evicts is set, in which case a write that would grow past capacity evicts the oldest cell instead of refusing (see Evicts). A slot-shaped row (see IsSlot) holds exactly one cell keyed SlotKey; a keyed row may hold any author-chosen keys except SlotKey itself, which is reserved for the value sugar and refused as an authored cell key.

observation.description: When a stored knowledge value was last seen and whether the latest observation still sees it.

visible.description: Whether the latest explicit refresh sees this cell.

min.description: The row-wide declared lower bound every cell's Value must satisfy, raw-encoded per Kind (raw FixedQ4816 bits for Fixed), or null for none. Present only together with Max — a range is authored as a pair or not at all. Legitimate only for Int/Fixed. Omitted from the wire when null.

max.description: The row-wide declared upper bound, raw-encoded per Kind, or null for none. Present only together with Min. Omitted from the wire when null.

capacity.description: The row's own cell-count ceiling (1..MaxCellsPerRow), or null to fall back to the implicit ceiling. A row declaring Capacity can never be a slot (IsSlot), even if it happens to carry exactly one cell — declaring a capacity is declaring table intent. Omitted from the wire when null.

nonNegative.description: Whether every cell's value must be non-negative, enforced regardless of any authored Min. Legitimate only for Int/Fixed. A timer is represented as Int with this set.

evicts.description: Whether this row is a bounded, FIFO-evicting table. Ordinarily a Capacity is a hard ceiling and a write that would exceed it is refused by name; with this set, such a write instead succeeds and, if it added a new key past capacity, evicts the row's oldest surviving cell. Eviction runs as a pure function of the candidate cells inside the compose step, so replay reproduces the identical victim, and the dropped key is named on the mutation's apply echo. Eviction is by insertion position, not recency of touch: a new key is appended to the end of Cells and eviction always drops index 0. Re-writing an existing key updates it in place without moving it — true FIFO, never LRU. Legitimate only together with a declared Capacity. Default false.

draw.description: The AUTHORED-RANDOMNESS facet: the declaration that a SITE's value is DRAWN rather than literal. One facet, one source family, one engine — an NPC-bark text site, a loot cell, a random census, and a drawn host backend are the SAME mechanism pointed at different sites.

source.description: The declared source to draw from, by name — or null when StateGenerator inlines one.
source.title: CellName

generator.description: An inline anonymous source — or null when Source names a declared one.

timing.description: When this site draws and whether it may be redrawn (see DrawTiming).
timing.title: DrawTiming

secret.description: An authority-provisioned 256-bit secret for an independently keyed streamDraw sample at each cursor. Never sent in observations.
secret.title: ClosedBitset256

skip.description: An authored seek, non-negative, default 0: a rebuild advances the generator by (skip + cursor) * cost rather than cursor * cost. Authored data, the same class as the seed ladder's own rungs — it never writes the persisted DrawCursor, which keeps counting samples from zero exactly as an unskipped site's does.

drawCursor.description: How many samples this site's Draw has ever consumed — engine-minted bookkeeping and the position the engine re-seeks to (GeneratorEngine.AdvancesPerSample scales it into Pcg32XshRr advances, so resuming is an exact O(1) advance rather than a replay of the earlier draws). Stored in the document, so world.undo, world.save, and replay rewind a site's draw position with the same whole-document restore that rewinds an ordinary counter. Zero when Draw is null; refused negative.

drawnMasks.description: This site's drawn masks — engine-minted bookkeeping a source under an exhausting GeneratorMode carries: one mask per context, by declaration ordinal, for a Markov source; exactly one for a weighted numeric source. Bit i is set when entry i has been drawn. Lives at the site rather than on the source row, which lets two sites reference one declared source and draw independently. Null or empty for a site whose source never exhausts.

historyCursor.description: How many values have ever been pushed into a Ring row — engine bookkeeping that names the next slot (cursor mod capacity) and how much of the ring is filled. Zero without the trait; refused negative.

knowledge.description: A persisted knowledge layer refreshed explicitly by the authority.

mask.description: A boolean board over the same topology; true cells are currently observed.

phase.description: Marks a plain integer row as a guarded submission stamp: the row's own generation Sequence, the sole state a PhaseGuard checks and the mutation pipeline advances. Nothing about who may act, in what order, or under what deadline is engine knowledge any more — a turn order, a round counter, a ready or skipped bitset, and a deadline are all ordinary rows a world's own rules author and advance, and eligibility is the ordinary grant/admission system over whichever rows a rule ties to this one via PhaseOf. Submitting any mutation whose PhaseGuard matches this generation both admits the submission and, on success, advances the generation by one: the guard's presence on a mutation IS the turn's completion, so a world that wants several ungated moves before a turn ends simply leaves those rows untagged and reserves PhaseOf for the one row that ends it.

sequence.description: The generation. Advanced by the mutation pipeline after a guarded mutation naming this row succeeds; never written directly.

phaseOf.description: The phase row required on external gameplay transforms that write this row.

valuesFrom.description: The discrete topology whose cell ordinals this row's integer values name — a value-typing trait, independent of Domain (legitimate only alongside a KeysOf domain over Int cells).

domain.description: A StateRow's declared cell domain — the closed answer to "which keys does this row's storage admit" that IsKeyed/IsSlot/CellCeiling switch over, replacing the five hand-kept discriminators (a null Board, Tokens, Zone, KeysFrom, or History facet) inference used to read the same shape off of. Orthogonal traits — a row's Advance/Dynamics/Cycle/ Draw/Visibility/Knowledge/ Phase/PhaseOf/ Evicts/Min/Max/ NonNegative — are unaffected by which case a row declares; every combination the validator already refused (a lattice row carrying advance, a phase row carrying capacity) is refused the identical way with the case substituted for the old field.

anyOf.description: One cell, keyed SlotKey — a scalar row. An omitted key addresses it. Carries no data, so InferDomain answers with the single Instance rather than allocating one per unauthored row.
anyOf.title: StateDomainSlot

anyOf.description: Explicit author-keyed cells (StateRow.Capacity and Cells carry the shape); no omitted-key address exists. The token-domain declaration row (the old dedicated tokens facet) is simply a row of this case whose Capacity is the domain's token-count ceiling — other rows address its keys through KeysOf rather than through a second facet of their own. Carries no data, so InferDomain answers with the single Instance rather than allocating one per unauthored keyed row.
anyOf.title: StateDomainKeys

anyOf.description: The row's key domain is another row's keys (see Keys). Ordered true gives the old zone semantics — cell order is pile order, first/last selection has gameplay meaning — while false gives the old plain keysFrom attribute-row semantics (a numeric fact per token, no pile order). The one shape two different authored roles used to spell as two different facets.

row.description: The row whose keys this row's own keys are drawn from.
row.title: CellName

ordered.description: Whether cell order carries gameplay meaning (a pile) rather than being incidental.

anyOf.title: StateDomainKeysOf

anyOf.description: One value per cell of a named state.lattices topology — the old board and lattice facets' shared shape. Which of the two storage strategies a row actually gets (sparse cells overlaying Empty, or the dense physical-field composite) is an implementation choice keyed on the row's own Kind — a Fixed row over a Field-kind topology compiles into the host's dense field storage, every other combination is the sparse board — never two authored traits.

topology.description: The state.lattices topology this row lies over.

empty.description: The value a sparse (board) cell reads before it is ever written; meaningless for the dense physical-field case, whose unwritten value is the field trait's own initial instead.

anyOf.title: StateDomainCellsOf

anyOf.description: The history ring: the row keeps the last Capacity pushed values in slots keyed 0..Capacity-1, oldest overwritten first — the old history facet.

capacity.description: How many pushes the ring keeps, 1..128.

empty.description: The value read for an age older than the ring holds.

anyOf.title: StateDomainRing

inverse.description: A CellsOf row's declared inverse: the board's cells are not authored directly but derived from a keyed Tokens row naming cells of the same topology and a Codes row keyed the same way, giving each token's code. Legitimate only on a Int row whose EffectiveDomain is CellsOf and that carries no field trait — a document project's validator enforces both.

tokens.description: The keyed Int row whose cell values name cells of the board's topology — a value naming no cell means that token is off the board.
tokens.title: CellName

codes.description: The row giving each token's code, keyed the same as Tokens — the same cell keys, in the same order, so index i of one names the same token as index i of the other.
codes.title: CellName

dynamics.description: The row's own (slot-cell) second-order easing trait, or null for an ordinary row whose slot value only changes through an explicit write. See StateDynamics. Legitimate only for Int/Fixed, only on a scalar (slot-eligible) row, and never together with Advance or Draw. A keyed row's own cells ease independently through Dynamics instead.

row.description: The referenced dynamics row name; must resolve.

y0.description: The follower's position at EpochTick as raw FixedQ4816 bits, independent of the carrying row's stored-value kind. Keeping the continuous state fixed-native preserves sub-unit phase when an integer target is rebased.

v0.description: The follower's velocity at EpochTick, per second, as raw FixedQ4816 bits. A sub-unit response kick therefore survives an integer-row rebase.

epochTick.description: The server tick Y0/V0 were captured at.

dynamics.title: StateDynamics

gatesDrive.description: Whether this row is a drive-admission gate. When set, this must be a keyed row (IsKeyed) whose per-body cell — keyed by the body's 0-based entity index — is consulted before admitting a drive or action intent for that body: a nonzero cell refuses the body's intents until the cell reads zero again, checked fresh every tick. The engine does not interpret the row's name; several independently named gate rows may exist at once, any one of which can refuse. Legitimate only on a row declaring Capacity, and only for Int/Fixed/ Bool. Default false.

field.description: A state row's field trait — carried only by a row whose Domain is CellsOf over a Field-kind topology: the row holds one Fixed scalar per cell of that topology instead of sparse board cells. Values are authored DECIMAL (like every lattice quantity), not raw Q48.16 bits; a field row refuses slot/keyed members (cells, capacity, advance, dynamics, draw -- per-cell draws are the spatial-draw seam, refused until it lands).

initial.description: The value every cell starts at before paint.

min.description: The least value a cell holds.

max.description: The greatest value a cell holds.

heightScale.description: World units of solid surface per unit of value above the lattice origin -- 0 for a row that is not geometry.

color.description: The color the row's surface shades with — a #RRGGBB literal or a state.<row>[.<key>] Text-cell binding (WorldColor's shared grammar, resolved live at emit); required when HeightScale is nonzero.

paint.description: The initial fills, applied in order over Initial.

items.description: One initial fill of a lattice row, applied in order over the row's initial. Every kind decides per CELL with integer hashes and Q48.16 arithmetic only, so a fill is bit-identical on every machine and backend -- lattice values are simulation state. The Field member is compile-stamped from the carrying row (see Compile) and omitted in the document.

anyOf.description: Every cell whose XZ centre lies in the rectangle takes Value.

minX.description: The rectangle's least X, world units.

minZ.description: The rectangle's least Z, world units.

maxX.description: The rectangle's greatest X, world units.

maxZ.description: The rectangle's greatest Z, world units.

field.description: Gets the filled row's name -- compile-stamped, never authored inside a trait.

anyOf.title: WorldLatticeFillRect

anyOf.description: Patchy fill: fixed-point hash-lattice fBm over the CELL INDEX decides each cell. Where the octave sum n (in [0, 1]) reaches Threshold, the cell takes Value · (n − Threshold) / (1 − Threshold) -- a smooth patch interior rising to the full value. The hash folds the fill's Seed with the world seed (the generation section's reroll lever), and every blend runs in Q48.16, so two boots of one document at one seed are bit-identical.

value.description: The peak value written inside a patch.

frequency.description: Lattice cells per noise cell reciprocal -- noise-cell edge in CELLS (e.g. 8 = one noise cell spans 8 lattice cells). At least 1.

threshold.description: The patch admission level in [0, 1); higher = sparser patches.

seed.description: The hash seed, folded with the world seed.

field.description: Gets the filled row's name -- compile-stamped, never authored inside a trait.

anyOf.title: WorldLatticeFillNoise

anyOf.description: Scattered discs: one jittered point per Spacing-cell block (integer-hash offset), and every cell within Radius cells of a point takes Value -- the CPU boot-fill sibling of the renderer's CellJitter scatter.

value.description: The value written inside each disc.

spacing.description: The scatter block edge in CELLS (at least 2).

radius.description: The disc radius in CELLS (at least 1; must leave the disc inside its block's jitter envelope, refused otherwise).

seed.description: The hash seed, folded with the world seed.

field.description: Gets the filled row's name -- compile-stamped, never authored inside a trait.

anyOf.title: WorldLatticeFillScatter

anyOf.description: Every cell drawn from a numeric authored-randomness source — the per-cell lattice draw. The fill is one pass of the row's own draw stream (seeded through the same ladder as a state-row site, under the row's state.<row> descriptor): cell k, in cell-index order, takes the sample a site at drawCursor + k would draw, so a weighted source under an exhausting mode draws its units across the field and restarts as it goes. The row's DrawCursor/DrawnMasks name the pass currently painted; generate <row> advances them one whole pass and repaints. Draw occupies its authored paint position (overwriting earlier fills and preceding later fills); boot, rebuild, load/reset, and a draw-rewinding undo repaint the pass the document names.

source.description: A declared generators row, or null when Generator is inlined.
source.title: CellName

generator.description: An inline numeric source, or null when Source is named.

field.description: Gets the filled row's name -- compile-stamped, never authored inside a trait.

anyOf.title: WorldLatticeFillDraw

items.title: WorldLatticeFill

medium.description: Marks this field a fluid MEDIUM, or null for an ordinary field. A medium field's value times HeightScale over the lattice origin is a free surface every active body samples each tick at its coupled cell — the same body-coupling ceiling Emit/ Expose resolve against — refused unless HeightScale is greater than zero (a surface-less medium is meaningless).
medium.title: WorldLatticeMedium

value.description: The decimal FixedQ4816 spelling (e.g. "12.5"), never raw bits.

min.description: The decimal FixedQ4816 spelling (e.g. "12.5"), never raw bits.

max.description: The decimal FixedQ4816 spelling (e.g. "12.5"), never raw bits.

value.description: The decimal FixedQ4816 spelling (e.g. "12.5"), never raw bits.

body.description: Per-body ephemeral counters and timers, compiled into each body's bounded ordinal arrays.

identity.description: Per-body counters and timers synchronized through the durable identity-document seam.

lattices.description: The lattice topologies the section's lattice-shaped rows lie over (see LatticeTopology; the document adds the physical WorldFieldTopology case).

items.description: One state.lattices topology — the footprint every lattice-shaped state row referencing it shares. The discrete cases are declared here, one per kind, each carrying only its own parameters — Radius, Band, and LayerHeight exist nowhere else. A host registers its dense Field case as a further derived record under the same $type discriminator. Kind is never authored directly; it is the discriminant every case's own JSON $type already carries, exposed as a property because so much of the compiler branches on it.

anyOf.description: A rectangular board, indexed by y times width plus x.

band.description: The vertical half-extent about the origin's Y a position must lie within to resolve to a cell (cellOf); 0 resolves any height, so a piece on the floor beneath a table still reads as on its square.

name.description: The topology's name — what a row's cellsOf domain references.

cellSize.description: The cubic cell edge, world units.

anyOf.title: LatticeTopologyGrid

anyOf.description: A cyclic sequence, indexed from zero — always wraps.

name.description: The topology's name — what a row's cellsOf domain references.

cellSize.description: The cubic cell edge, world units.

anyOf.title: LatticeTopologyRing

anyOf.description: A hexagonal disk of the given radius, indexed in HexagonalIndex order: rings outward from the origin, consecutive indices adjacent.

name.description: The topology's name — what a row's cellsOf domain references.

cellSize.description: The cubic cell edge, world units.

anyOf.title: LatticeTopologyHex

anyOf.description: A box of width by layers by depth cells with the 26 space directions, indexed by (layer times depth plus z) times width plus x.

layerHeight.description: The world-space height of one layer, so a position's Y above the origin resolves to a layer the way X and Z resolve to a column; positive.

name.description: The topology's name — what a row's cellsOf domain references.

cellSize.description: The cubic cell edge, world units.

anyOf.title: LatticeTopologyBox

anyOf.description: An explicit graph. Cell i is cells[i]; its centre is relative to origin in world units, and cellSize is the resolution radius — a position within half a cell size of a centre resolves to it, nearest first. Every direction is a slot: an edge from a cell along a direction fills that slot, and unless OneWay also fills the destination's slot along the direction's opposite, so a cell with k neighbours needs k distinct directions among its edges. Symmetry is the identity alone.

id.description: The id edges name it by; distinct within the graph.

centre.description: The centre, relative to the topology's origin, in world units.

directions.description: The direction slots, each naming its opposite (possibly itself).

items.description: One direction slot of a Graph.

name.description: The direction's name, as rules and patterns spell it.

opposite.description: The direction an edge is followed back along; a symmetric link names itself.

items.title: GraphDirection

items.description: One edge of a Graph: From reaches To along Direction, and unless OneWay, To reaches From along the direction's opposite.

oneWay.description: Whether the reverse edge is left unfilled (a ladder, a one-way street).

items.title: GraphEdge

name.description: The topology's name — what a row's cellsOf domain references.

cellSize.description: The cubic cell edge, world units.

anyOf.title: LatticeTopologyGraph

anyOf.description: A tiling generated within a radius — the tiles whose centres lie within radius edge lengths of the origin, cellSize being the edge length in world units. It is the GraphGenerate materializes: cell i is the i-th tile outward from the origin, directions are the edge normals by angle (a0, a30, …, counterclockwise from +X), and a position resolves to the nearest tile centre within half an edge. The symmetry group is the identity.

radius.description: The patch radius in edge lengths, at least 1.

name.description: The topology's name — what a row's cellsOf domain references.

cellSize.description: The cubic cell edge, world units.

anyOf.title: LatticeTopologyTiling

anyOf.description: The physical state.lattices topology: a scalar field over the lattice's footprint, evolved by reactions each StepEveryTicks — the document's own case of LatticeTopology, registered under the field discriminator beside the engine's discrete cases.

layers.description: Cells along +Y -- 1 is a ground lattice.

reactions.description: The per-step reactions, applied in document order.

items.description: One reaction — a local rule every cell (or every tagged body) applies each lattice step. Reactions run in document order; Diffuse reads the previous step's values for the whole field, every other kind reads and writes cells in place, row-major.

anyOf.description: Moves each cell a fraction of the way toward the mean of its face neighbours (four on a ground lattice, six in a volume).
anyOf.title: WorldReactionDiffuse

anyOf.description: Scales each cell toward zero: v -= v·rate.
anyOf.title: WorldReactionDecay

anyOf.description: Where every condition holds at a cell, applies every write at that cell — ignition, melting, evaporation, freezing are rows of this shape.

when.description: The conditions, all of which must hold.

items.description: One per-cell condition of a Transform.

field.description: The field read at the cell.

value.description: The scalar compared against (literal or state-row reference).
value.title: WorldLatticeScalar

items.title: WorldFieldCondition

items.description: One per-cell write of a Transform.

field.description: The field written at the cell.

value.description: The constant written or added; the result clamps to the field's range.
value.title: WorldLatticeScalar

items.title: WorldFieldWrite

anyOf.title: WorldReactionTransform

anyOf.description: Every active body whose cell in the keyed state row Tag reads nonzero adds Amount to Field at the cell it occupies — a burning body is a heat source.

tag.description: The keyed int state row whose nonzero cells name the emitting bodies.

amount.description: The amount per step; the cell clamps to the field's range.
amount.title: WorldLatticeScalar

anyOf.title: WorldReactionEmit

anyOf.description: Writes 1 or 0 into Row's cell for every active body, by whether Field at the body's cell satisfies the comparison — a body standing in a burning cell becomes tagged, and body-level chemistry takes it from there.

field.description: The field sampled at the body.

row.description: The keyed int state row written, keyed by body index.

anyOf.title: WorldReactionExpose

anyOf.description: Moves Field downhill, cell to cell, over the combined surface height of Over plus Field's own value -- mass-conserving except where a cell's clamp to its declared [min, max] binds. Every cell donates an equal share of its previous-step value to each of the lattice's active-axis directions (four on a ground lattice, six in a volume -- the SAME count for every cell, whether a direction reaches a neighbour or the lattice edge), and sends that share only along a direction that is strictly downhill; a level or uphill direction moves nothing.

rate.description: The fraction of a cell's per-direction share that actually moves each step, in [0, 1].
rate.title: WorldLatticeScalar

over.description: The other lattice rows forming the terrain basis a downhill direction is measured against; empty or omitted means the field flows over its own height alone.

spillRow.description: The scalar fixed-kind state row an edge cell's outward share accumulates into each step (a clamped add), or null to treat every lattice edge as a wall.

anyOf.title: WorldReactionFlow

items.title: WorldReaction

name.description: The topology's name — what a row's cellsOf domain references.

cellSize.description: The cubic cell edge, world units.

anyOf.title: WorldFieldTopology

items.title: LatticeTopology
